newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in boxed-range after rebound.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in boxed-range after rebound.

text.p: The ringgit was trapped in a boxed range against the dollar throughout Asian trading after rebounding from Wednesday's fall, dealers said.
The Malaysian market was closed on Thursday for a holiday.
Dealers said the ringgit rebound came on the back of the dollar's sharp fall against the yen.
"Except for some position adjustment, there was really not much activity today," said a dealer with a foreign bank.
Dealers said the ringgit also benefited from the easing of uncertainties following clarification from Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on his intended vacation.

Reports that Mahathir is taking an unprecedented two-month vacation starting this month, leaving his deputy Anwar Ibrahim in his place, sparked off political concerns and unnerved the market on Wednesday.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5065/75 to the dollar against 2.5125/35 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
However, the ringgit fell to 2.0420/36 per 100 yen from 2.0251/63 previously.
Dealers said there was talk of Japanese repatriating funds from the ringgit back into the yen following the recovery of the Japanese currency.
